rules.sdk: iOS 27 SDK (checked with Xcode 27.1, 27A9275, on the iOS 27.0 and iOS 26.4 simulators)

verdict.text: The Liquid Glass opt-out is ignored when built with the iOS 27 SDK; 2 custom styles to review first

findings.title: Liquid Glass opt-out that the iOS 27 SDK ignores
findings.message: ios.infoPlist sets UIDesignRequiresCompatibility to true in app.json.

fix.title: Remove the opt-out from the Expo config and rebuild the native project
steps: Delete UIDesignRequiresCompatibility from ios.infoPlist in the Expo config.
Run npx expo prebuild --clean -p ios (or let EAS Build do it) so the generated Info.plist no longer has it.
Run the app on an iOS 27 simulator; the other findings in this report are the places to look at first.

findings.title: Native stack header with its own background

fix.title: Leave the header background to the system on iOS
steps: Set headerStyle.backgroundColor, headerBackground and headerBlurEffect only for Android (Platform.select) or for iOS before 26.
Keep the brand colour on headerTintColor.

findings.title: Native stack header with its own background

fix.title: Leave the header background to the system on iOS
steps: Set headerStyle.backgroundColor, headerBackground and headerBlurEffect only for Android (Platform.select) or for iOS before 26.

findings.title: Tab bar drawn in JavaScript
findings.message: Expo Router's Tabs draws the tab bar in JavaScript.

fix.title: Move to Expo Router's native tabs, or keep the JavaScript bar on purpose
steps: For the system tab bar, use NativeTabs from expo-router/native-tabs (SDK 58 and later; expo-router/unstable-native-tabs in SDK 54 to 57).
If the custom bar is part of the brand, keep it and check it next to the Liquid Glass headers on an iOS 27 simulator.
